Unexpected Selectivity of Intramolecular [3+2] Cycloaddition of
Trimethylenemethane (TMM) Diyl toward Total Synthesis of
Conidiogenone B
Myungjo J. Kim, [a,b] Sanghyeon Lee,[a] Taek Kang,[a] Mu-Hyun Baik,* [b,a] and
Hee-Yoon Lee*[a]
Abstract: In the course of a study toward a total synthesis of
conidiogenone B through TMM diyl-mediated tandem cyclo-
addition reaction, unexpected regioselectivity for a bridged iso-
mer was observed. The synthetic and computational studies
Introduction
Total synthesis of natural products with complex structural fea-
tures, especially with contiguous all-carbon quaternary centers,
have challenged synthetic chemistry community since the
dawn of the 20
th century[1] and triggered development of vari-
ous synthetic methodologies and strategies. [2] Among synthetic
strategies for the construction of structurally c ongested natural
products, trimethylenemethane (TMM) diyl-mediated tandem
cycloaddition reaction proved particularly attractive, as it has
offered efficient means to construct all-carbon quaternary cen-
ters at ring junctions and rapid access to architectural complex-
ity through the tandem process.
[3] From the viewpoint of “ideal
synthesis”,[4] this cascade process involving the successive intra-
molecular [3+2] cycloaddition reactions to form three rings at
once is attractive because it is highly step-, and pot-economical.
We have successfully applied this synthetic methodology to the
total synthesis of highly congested natural products possessing
triquinane structure (Figure 1).
Total syntheses of various triquinanes were executed
through TMM diyl [3+2] cycloaddition reaction, and complex
natural products with multiple quaternary centers were suc-
cessfully synthesized through the TMM diyl-mediated tandem
cycloaddition reaction. Following these successful examples, we
were to extend the synthetic st rategy to the total synthesis of
another challenging structure of tetracyclic diterpene, conidio-

To understand the source of the selectivity, the cycloaddition
reaction of model system was studied as shown in Table 1.
Effect of another methyl group on the TMM diyl was compared
to the one with only one methyl group on the TMM diyl. Intra-
molecular [3+2] cycloaddition of the dimethyl-substituted TMM
diyl 25 resulted in the exclusive formation of the bridged prod-
uct 26. In comparison, monomethyl-substituted TMM diyl 27,
showed the exclusive production of linear product 28. This re-
sult clearly indicated that selectivity for the bridged product
was greatly influenced by the presence of the second methyl
group on the TMM diyl. Formation of the bridged cycloaddition
product from TMM diyl cycloaddition reaction has been re-
ported in the past by changing steric environment on the olefin
moiety, and different electronic and steric environment for the
cycloaddition reaction altered the selectivity (Table 2).

the cycloaddition reaction and could be capable of predicting
selectivity of the reaction. Therefore, we calculated the actual

In the case of 25 and 27, cycloaddition barriers were esti-
mated to be 16.3 and 11.1 kcal/mol, respectively, implying that
the extra methyl group of 25 played a crucial role to dictate
the reaction pathway. This difference of 5.2 kcal/mol is signifi-

group is very close to the bond forming carbon and leads to a
more pronounced structural distortion characterized by a C–C
distance of 2.53 Å ( 25-TS), which is notably longer than 2.31 Å
that is seen in 27-TS. Although the cycloaddition is formally
synchronous, the optimized transition state structures reveal a
significant degree of asynchronous nature with the two proxi-
mal C–C distances of 2.78 and 2.93 Å being notably longer than
the distal C–C distances. Intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) cal-
culations indeed showed a clear shoulder
[17] for 27-TS, which
is found for a highly asynchronous process (see Supporting
Information). Our calculations for the singlet pathway pre-

of magnitude slower than that of 27, and thus facilitated the
complete intersystem crossing to triplet and selectively af-
forded the bridged product 26 due to the steric hindrance im-

With this information, we anticipated that the electronic ef-
fect on the olefin moiety might override the steric bias from
the extra methyl group on the TMM moiety for the cycloaddi-
tion through the singlet pathway dominant. We first conducted
a computational study of TMM diyl 32 bearing both an EWG
on the olefin moiety and the extra methyl group on TMM diyl

part, as well as its singlet cycloaddition transition state 32-
TS.[18] The calculated cycloaddition barrier for 32 was estimated
to be 10.0 kcal/mol which is considerably lower than those of
25 and 27 by 6.3 and 1.1 kcal/mol. From this comparison, we
anticipated that linear isomer 33 could be obtained from 32
(Scheme 5). To verify the prediction from the calculation, we
prepared TMM diyl precursor 31, and examined the tandem
cycloaddition reaction via TMM diyl 32. The tandem cycloaddi-
tion of 31 via TMM diyl 32 indeed resulted in the linear product
33, albeit in low yield presumably due to the decomposition of
the fragile vinyl sulfone. This result assured that addition of an
EWG to the olefin moiety can override the selectivity for the
bridged isomer arose from the extra methyl group on the TMM
diyl moiety.
Scheme 5. Verification of prediction from energy calculation.
These results strongly indicate that preference of intramolec-
ular cycloaddition of a TMM diyl with an olefin could be pre-
dicted and controlled, as the regioselectivity is governed by the
electronic and steric factors on both the olefin and the TMM
diyl. These factors control the kinetics of the intramolecular
[3+2] cycloaddition reaction of TMM diyls. When there is low
steric influence during the cycloaddition reaction, the linear iso-
mer would be the major product regardless of the spin state of
the TMM diyl. When the cycloaddition barrier is lowered by the
electronic effect, the singlet TMM diyl would undergo cyclo-
addition reaction to form exclusively the linear isomer before
the intersystem crossing into the triplet TMM diyl would take
place. In the case of 32, it was confirmed that stabilizing the
LUMO
Olefin could overcome the steric clash from the extra
methyl substituent at the TMM diyl. These results hinted that
the total synthesis of conidiogenone B through tandem cyclo-
addition reaction via TMM diyl could be feasible as modification
of the substrate for the cy cloaddition that should alter the elec-
tronic environment of the olefin moiety to shift the reactivity
in favor of the desired linear product.
Conclusions
Toward the total synthesis of conidiogenone B, the precursor
for the tandem cycloaddition reaction via TMM diyl was pre-
pared from Wieland–Miescher ketone 1 through Eschenmoser–
Tanabe fragmentation and Wang allenation. Unexpected regio-
selectivity of the cycloaddition for a bridged isomer was ob-
tained from the tandem cycloaddition reaction, which led us to
explore the intrinsic nature of the electronic and steric effect
for selectivity of cycloaddition by synthetic and computational
model studies. We obtained some valuable conclusions from
the model studies as follows. (1) An extra methyl group on TMM
diyl moiety significantly reduc es the rate of the singlet cyclo-
addition reaction and exerted enough steric interaction for the

exclusive formation of the bridged isomer via triplet pathway.
(2) EWG on the olefin moiety renders the cycloaddition through
singlet pathway relatively faster than intersystem crossing to
produce the linear isomer. (3) This electronic effect by an addi-
tional EWG on the olefin moiety could even override the steric
interaction from the second extra methyl group on the TMM
diyl to yield the linear isomer. It is also notable that there have
been only a handful of examples with regioselectivity for a
bridged cycloaddition product,
[8b,14,19] and the current study re-
veals that the selectivity between linear isomer and bridged
isomer could be controlled by altering the substituents on the
TMM diyl and/or the olefin.
